fact_text: Pakistan's energy circular debt reached about PKR 5.3 trillion by June 2026, up from about PKR 2.5 trillion in 2025.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The power sector's circular debt stood at about PKR 1.65 trillion in the report's snapshot.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The gas sector's circular debt was about PKR 3.6 trillion in the report's snapshot.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Of the gas-sector circular debt, about PKR 1.8 trillion is principal and about PKR 1.7 trillion is late payment surcharge.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Circular debt cycle: when consumers stop paying or cannot afford bills, and theft and line losses at distribution companies rise, distributors pay late, so oil and gas producers' payments are delayed.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The Petroleum Division sent a gas circular debt settlement plan of about PKR 1.5 trillion to the Cabinet Committee on Energy.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The proposed settlement plan would raise PKR 540 billion from dividends of OGDCL, PPL and Government Holding (Private) Limited.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The settlement plan includes PKR 70 billion from a petroleum development levy on petrol and diesel per litre.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The settlement plan expects PKR 670 billion of savings from lower RLNG cargo purchases and price recovery.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Textile exports fell by about USD 1.5 billion from 2022 and stood at about USD 17.93 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Total Pakistani exports fell by about USD 9.5 billion from 2022 to about USD 30 billion.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Pakistani exporters pay about 12 to 13 cents per unit of energy, against about 6 to 9 cents in competing locations.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The reporter argued that high energy costs, the main driver of production cost, stop Pakistani exporters from competing in world markets.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Independent power producers under 1994 take-or-pay style contracts are paid for 100 percent of capacity even when they produce as little as 20 percent of it.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The 1994 power policy, backed by the IMF and ADB, drew 17 independent power producers, and Chinese generation companies joined by 2010.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Installed generation capacity reached about 45,000 MW, while electricity consumption has not reached 20,000 MW.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The reporter said capacity charges keep rising and the government passes that burden to the public through tariffs.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Two existing LNG terminals are heavily under-utilised, yet consumers pay capacity payments of about PKR 55 million a day for them.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Qatar supplied about 90 percent of Pakistan's LNG, and that supply has nearly stopped after the Strait of Hormuz closure.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Gas makes up about 30 percent of Pakistan's electricity generation.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Pakistan became the largest importer of solar panels from China in 2024, and imported solar systems are easing grid demand for households and industry.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: When users leave the grid for their own power, the fixed capacity charges shift onto the remaining grid users, raising their bills.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Rising Neelum-Jhelum project costs are passed to consumers through a Neelum-Jhelum surcharge on bills.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The reporter argued that World Bank-backed hydropower projects bring upstream-downstream disputes, population displacement and Indus delta water shortages.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: Pakistan still relies on furnace oil and coal plants for power, which the reporter linked to shortages, load-shedding and overbilling.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The reporter argued that energy policies backed by the IMF, World Bank and ADB were unstable and made without proper consultation, helping create the circular debt.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The textile sector is described as the backbone of Pakistan's manufacturing and exports.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)

fact_text: The reporter said the public absorbs the circular debt cost through high electricity and gas prices, while households cut back on energy use.
source_name: Nukta Business, 'Pakistan’s Circular Debt Hits PKR 5.3 Trillion: Who Pays the Price? | Nukta Business' (YouTube, 2026-10-02)
